/* Dock control styles — thin @import root over controls/*.css
   Split into per-control partials (no god-module).
 *
 * dock.css keeps the shell / density / grain / layer-crossfade contract + the
 * shared cross-control four-state contract (the `:focus-visible` / `:disabled`
 * comma-groups + the motion-token `:where()` group, which reference these
 * control selectors but are shared, not per-control). This file owns the FIVE
 * control families themselves, split into cohesive partials each under the
 * 500-line bound, @import-ed below in CASCADE ORDER into the SAME
 * `@layer components` (the carve moves rules across files in the same source
 * position → byte-isomorphic dist):
 *   1. dock-controls/icon-button.css      `.dock-icon-button` (base / states / glyph / --compact)
 *   2. dock-controls/tab-button.css       `.dock-tab-button` (base / tier-primary / tier-secondary)
 *   3. dock-controls/triggers.css         `.dock-select-trigger` / `.dock-dropdown-trigger` (base / states / __chevron)
 *   4. dock-controls/touch-floor.css      the coarse @media touch floor + the vertical-dock SELECTED register
 *
 * The shared cross-family `:where()` group (the small-tile specular sizing
 * re-point) stays at THIS root — exactly as the dock.css carve kept its shared
 * `:where()` four-state contract at ITS root — because it references every
 * control selector and nesting it under one control would change coverage.
 *
 * The per-family parent+state clusters use native `&`-nesting
 * (Baseline Widely available 2023; Lightning CSS down-compiles so the shipped
 * `dist` CSS is flat with IDENTICAL specificity). The cross-family comma-groups
 * stay UN-nested (nesting under one control would change coverage).
 *
 * Imported by index.css directly after dock.css in the same `@layer components`
 * (cascade rung 6b) — no new subpath; it ships inside `/styles`.
 *
 * CSS `@import` rules must precede every other rule (the dock.css precedent),
 * so the five family partials @import FIRST; the shared cross-family `:where()`
 * group follows in its own `@layer components`. The `:where()` group has ZERO
 * specificity and sets `--glass-specular-size` on the control family — no family
 * partial re-sets that property, so its source position (after the imports vs
 * before) is cascade-immaterial; the byte-isomorphism witness (§4) is the arbiter. */
@import "./icon-button.css";
@import "./tab-button.css";
@import "./triggers.css";
@import "./touch-floor.css";

@layer components {
    /* ~~The draggable-item GRAB squish. A grabbed dock item (`.glass-drag-lift`, written
       by useDockItemDrag while the gesture is in flight) deforms with the
       volume-preserving `--stretch` register … Horizontal docks stretch X / compress Y;
       vertical stretch Y / compress X.~~ — [2026-08-10 · BK #47 · R-E, ALL DOCK DRAG
       STRUCK] The two rules that stood here are DELETED. They are the dock's last drag
       bytes, and they were already dead.

       THE DETECTOR, verbatim, this seat:
         `grep -rn "dock-items-draggable" src/ demo/ tests/` → 2 hits, and BOTH were
              these two selectors. The class had ZERO emitters — no SFC, no story, no
              test ever wrote it, so neither rule could match on any tree.
         `grep -rn "useDockItemDrag" src/` → 1 hit, the PROSE above. The composable the
              comment named as the live writer of `.glass-drag-lift` does not exist.

       So this was a mechanism documented in the present tense, gated on a class nothing
       sets, driven by a composable that was never on disk. Deleting it is not a
       behaviour change — no computed style can differ — which is why it lands here
       rather than waiting on paint.

       GF-DOCK R-E rules the merits independently: ALL drag on the dock is struck (the
       PASS3 lens, the protrusion/outside-clip layer, and the residual block-axis drag).
       Under `touch-action: pan-x` the inline gesture belongs to the scroller, and a
       block-axis drag on a route dock has no named commit semantics. Commit is
       tap/click/keyboard.

       NOT touched, and deliberately: `.glass-drag-lift` itself is LIVE on the layer
       SWITCHER (`DockLayerGroup.vue:270`, with `.glass-drag-grabbable` at :230) and its
       rules live in `src/components/tabs/styles/drag.css`. That is the switcher's drag,
       not dock-item drag, and it is out of this strike's scope and out of the fence. */

    /* Momentum-gated dock-control press spring. The `:active` squish
       toward `--scale-press-dock` settles on a NO-OVERSHOOT spring (Apple,
       "Designing Fluid Interfaces": default 100% damping — no bounce — for a tap;
       reserve bounce for surfaces driven by gesture MOMENTUM). The dock controls
       are tap surfaces (no momentum).

       The per-surface re-point of `--dock-press-spring` is DELETED here: the ROOT
       token (`tokens.css`) IS the doctrine register, so the re-point was a dead
       byte-identical redeclaration — the exact per-surface fork the doctrine claims
       to have killed. The dock controls inherit the press register straight from the
       ROOT token; this `:where()` group keeps ONLY the small-tile specular sizing
       below. */
    :where(
        .dock-icon-button,
        .dock-tab-button,
        .dock-select-trigger,
        .dock-dropdown-trigger
    ) {
        /* The small-tile specular sizing. The dock controls are
           ~40px tiles, a fraction of a card's plate, so the global 36% specular
           radius blooms a tile-filling disc (the finding). The family re-points
           `--glass-specular-size` to the tighter `--dock-control-specular-size` (22%,
           tokens.css), so the SHARED material-group `::before` catch-light recipe
           (glass.css) paints a restrained EDGE-catch on the small tile WITHOUT
           forking the recipe — the gleam wakes on hover/active (the cohort's 0.1/0.16
           rungs), sized for the tile. The rest intensity stays 0 (the default-off
           discipline) so the resting tile carries NO bloom. */
        --glass-specular-size: var(--dock-control-specular-size, 22%);
    }
}
